title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
prompt:
Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence (elements in order, not necessarily contiguous).

**Example**: `[10,9,2,5,3,7,101,18]` → `4` (e.g. `[2,3,7,101]`).

The O(n log n) approach keeps a `tails` array where `tails[k]` is the smallest possible tail of an increasing subsequence of length k+1; binary-search each number into it.
hints: Maintain `tails`: the smallest tail value for an LIS of each length.
For each number, binary-search the first tail ≥ it; replace it (or append if it's largest so far).
The length of `tails` is the LIS length. (An O(n²) dp with dp[i] = best ending at i also works.)

solution.explanation: `tails` stays sorted; `tails[k]` being the smallest achievable tail for length k+1 means a new number either extends the longest run (append) or improves a shorter run's tail (replace), keeping future options maximally open. The binary search makes it O(n log n) — `tails` isn't the LIS itself, but its length is correct.
